title: Composition and identity normalization of the specified shriek product map
statement:
Use the finite-field datum, finite ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and actual constructible operations of [sk-def-sf-operations], on separated finite-type $k$-schemes. For $i=1,2$ let $X_i\xrightarrow{f_i}Y_i\xrightarrow{g_i}S_i$ be separated finite-type morphisms. Put $F=f_1\times_k f_2$, $G=g_1\times_k g_2$, and $h_i=g_if_i$. Write $P_u=Ru_!$, with its specified compact-support composition comparisons. For $B_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$, let
$$t_{f_1,f_2}(B_1,B_2):P_F(B_1\boxtimes B_2)\longrightarrow P_{f_1}B_1\boxtimes P_{f_2}B_2$$
be precisely the $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ isomorphism of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i), constructed from the relative product map and the compact-support base-change identifications. Under the specified identifications $P_{GF}=P_GP_F$ and $P_{h_i}=P_{g_i}P_{f_i}$, one has the equality
$$t_{h_1,h_2}(B_1,B_2)=t_{g_1,g_2}(P_{f_1}B_1,P_{f_2}B_2)\circ P_G\bigl(t_{f_1,f_2}(B_1,B_2)\bigr).$$
For $f_i=\operatorname{id}_{X_i}$, the identity comparisons identify $t_{f_1,f_2}(B_1,B_2)$ with $\operatorname{id}_{B_1\boxtimes B_2}$.

source.place: canonical composition/PF/base-change formula in steps (1)--(4), and coherence paragraph: composition normalization needed when iterating that formula; identity-square normalization

proof.text: Write $U_u=Lu^*$, $P_u=Ru_!$, and $D_u(M,L)=\operatorname{PF}_{u,M,L}^{-1}$. All maps below are the compactification-defined maps of [def-exchange-projection], with the canonical compositor $P_vP_u\cong P_{vu}$. The pullbacks, tensors and compact-support images of the inputs remain in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i),(ii),(iv). Their etale-origin witnesses exist by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), so the composition and exchange-pasting assertions apply. Projection maps are invertible by [fix-prop-projection-formula]; compact-support exchanges are invertible by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Use the monoidal and signed symmetry comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] throughout. This verifies the domains before taking any inverse; no axiomatic six-functor datum is assumed.

For $u:T\to V$ and an auxiliary scheme $Z$, put $\bar u=u\times1_Z$, with projections $r:T\times Z\to T$, $s:V\times Z\to V$, $z:V\times Z\to Z$. Let $E_{u,Z}(M):U_sP_uM\to P_{\bar u}U_rM$ be exchange. Define the first-factor map
$$L_{u,Z}(M,N)=(E_{u,Z}(M)^{-1}\otimes1)D_{\bar u}(U_rM,U_zN).$$
It goes from $P_{\bar u}(M\boxtimes N)$ to $P_uM\boxtimes N$. Define $R_{Z,u}(N,M)$ by conjugating $L_{u,Z}(M,N)$ with the swaps of product schemes and the signed tensor symmetries. Thus $R$ applies $P_u$ in the second factor; the source $P_{1_Z\times u}$ is identified with the swap-conjugate of $P_{u\times1_Z}$ by the canonical compositors with the swap isomorphisms [thm-sf-comp-composition]. These are abbreviations for displayed composites, not additional comparison data. In particular, this fixes the order of all inverse projection and exchange factors that will occur in the product calculation.

source.place: canonical PF/base-change composite and coherence paragraph: concrete inverse base-change equation

proof.text:
For $u:T\to V$, $v:W\to Z$, set $a=u\times1_Z:T\times Z\to V\times Z$, $b=1_V\times v:V\times W\to V\times Z$, and $a'=u\times1_W$. Apply [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i) over $V\times Z$ with inputs pulled back from $M$ on $T$ and $N$ on $W$. The formula of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] is, in its stated direction, inverse compositor, $P_bD_{a'}$, $P_b(E_{a,b}^{-1}\otimes1)$, symmetry, $D_b$, symmetry. This is $t_{u,v}$ itself, not its inverse. Write $s:V\times Z\to V$, $s':V\times W\to V$, $q:V\times W\to W$, and $K=U_{T\times Z\to T}M$. Horizontal exchange pasting [fix-lem-exchanges] gives
$$E_{a,b}(K)\,U_bE_{u,Z}(M)=E_{u,W}(M).$$
Replace $P_aK$ by $U_sP_uM$ through $E_{u,Z}^{-1}$. Naturality of the outer inverse PF moves that replacement past $D_b$. The first inverse PF and the two successive inverse exchanges now give $L_{u,W}$. The remaining arrows are precisely
$$P_b(U_{s'}P_uM\otimes U_qN)\xrightarrow{P_b\sigma}P_b(U_qN\otimes U_bU_sP_uM)\xrightarrow{D_b}P_bU_qN\otimes U_sP_uM\xrightarrow{E_{v,V}^{-1}\otimes1,\,\sigma}P_uM\boxtimes P_vN,$$
namely $R_{V,v}$. Thus
$$t_{u,v}(M,N)=R_{V,v}(P_uM,N)P_bL_{u,W}(M,N). \tag{F}$$

source.place: steps (1)--(4): specialize the relative map to the product base and identify its six arrows

proof.text:
For $T\xrightarrow uV\xrightarrow vS$ and fixed $Z$, put $A=u\times1_Z$, $B=v\times1_Z$, $H=U_{T\times Z\to T}M$, $Q=U_{S\times Z\to Z}N$. The inverse composition equation of [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate], using the compositor of [thm-sf-comp-composition], is
$$D_{BA}(H,Q)=D_B(P_AH,Q)\,P_BD_A(H,U_BQ).$$
Expand $L_{v,Z}(P_uM,N)P_BL_{u,Z}(M,N)$. Naturality of $D_B$ moves $P_B(E_{u,Z}^{-1}\otimes1)$ to the left of $D_B$; the resulting expression is
$$((E_{v,Z}^{-1}P_u)\circ P_BE_{u,Z}^{-1}\ \otimes1)\,D_B(P_AH,Q)\,P_BD_A(H,U_BQ).$$
Vertical exchange pasting [fix-lem-exchanges] identifies the first parenthesis with $E_{vu,Z}^{-1}$. The displayed inverse PF composition identity identifies the remaining two factors with $D_{BA}$. Therefore
$$L_{vu,Z}(M,N)=L_{v,Z}(P_uM,N)\,P_{v\times1_Z}L_{u,Z}(M,N). \tag{L}$$
This uses compatible compactifications for $u,v$ in the cited mate identity; the specified compositor and compactification independence identify it with the chosen operations. Such a triangle is provided by [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle].

source.place: coherence paragraph: composition of the first-factor projection/exchange maps

proof.text:
Conjugate (L) by the product swaps and tensor symmetries used to define $R$. The two adjacent swaps are inverse and cancel; naturality of symmetry moves them through the functorial images. The transport of $P$, $D$ and $E$ along the swap isomorphisms of product schemes is compatible with composition: the compositors with the swaps reassociate by the associativity clause of [thm-sf-comp-composition], the projection maps are compatible with that composition law by [fix-prop-projection-formula], and the exchanges respect the morphisms of square data given by the swaps and paste vertically by [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(2). This gives the second-factor composition equation
$$R_{Z,vu}(N,M)=R_{Z,v}(N,P_uM)\,P_{1_Z\times v}R_{Z,u}(N,M). \tag{R}$$
All signs are the signs of the same derived tensor symmetry; its compatibility with pullback composition is part of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso].

source.place: coherence paragraph: the second-factor version of the preceding composition calculation

proof.text:
Here is the mixed interchange, with all four morphisms specified:
$$\begin{array}{ccc}T\times W&\xrightarrow{u\times1_W}&V\times W\\ {1_T\times v}\downarrow&&\downarrow{1_V\times v}\\ T\times Z&\xrightarrow{u\times1_Z}&V\times Z.\end{array}$$
For $M$ on $T$, $N$ on $W$, the equation is
$$R_{V,v}(P_uM,N)P_{1_V\times v}L_{u,W}(M,N)
=L_{u,Z}(M,P_vN)P_{u\times1_Z}R_{T,v}(M,N). \tag{I}$$
The two sources are identified by the canonical compositors, since both total maps are $u\times v$. To check the specified arrows, take the relative product data $a:T\times Z\to V\times Z$, $b:V\times W\to V\times Z$ from Step 3, with their pulled-back inputs. Formula (F) expands its relative product map as the left side of (I). Now interchange $a,b$. Clause (i), symmetry, in the statement of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] identifies the swapped relative map, followed by target tensor symmetry, with the original map. Expanding that swapped map gives the right side of (I): its inner $D$ is for $1_T\times v$, its outer $D$ is for $u\times1_Z$, and naturality of the outer inverse PF and horizontal exchange pasting, exactly as in Step 3, identify their coefficient exchanges with $R_{T,v}$ and $L_{u,Z}$. The source swap is precisely the canonical fibre-product swap. Thus this is the mixed PF/base-change identity for the displayed product square. The non-elementary equality used here is the existing relative theorem's explicit symmetry clause, not an inference from separate composition laws or an assumed six-functor coherence axiom.

source.place: coherence paragraph (i): symmetry of the relative product map, applied to the specified mixed square

proof.text:
Put $A_i=P_{f_i}B_i$, and name the four consecutive product maps
$$d=f_1\times1_{X_2},\quad a=g_1\times1_{X_2},\quad b=1_{S_1}\times f_2,\quad c=1_{S_1}\times g_2.$$
Also put $a'=g_1\times1_{Y_2}$ and $b'=1_{Y_1}\times f_2$; thus $ba=a'b'$ and $GF=cbad=ca'b'd$. Substituting (L) and (R) in (F) for $(h_1,h_2)$ gives
$$t_h=R_{S_1,g_2}(P_{g_1}A_1,A_2)\,P_c\bigl(R_{S_1,f_2}(P_{g_1}A_1,B_2)P_bL_{g_1,X_2}(A_1,B_2)\bigr)\,P_{cba}L_{f_1,X_2}(B_1,B_2).$$
Apply (I) with $u=g_1$, $v=f_2$, $M=A_1$, $N=B_2$ to the parenthesis. The expression becomes
$$\bigl(R_{S_1,g_2}(P_{g_1}A_1,A_2)P_cL_{g_1,Y_2}(A_1,A_2)\bigr)\,P_{ca'}\bigl(R_{Y_1,f_2}(A_1,B_2)P_{b'}L_{f_1,X_2}(B_1,B_2)\bigr).$$
The first parenthesis is $t_g(A_1,A_2)$ by (F); the second is $t_f(B_1,B_2)$ by (F), and $ca'=G$. This proves exactly $t_h=t_g\circ P_G(t_f)$. Associativity of the canonical compositor in [thm-sf-comp-composition] identifies all the displayed multi-stage functor composites with the identifications in the statement.

proof.text: For $u=1_T$, choose the identity compactification $j=p=1_T$ in [def-exchange-projection]. Its proper projection map is the identity by [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition]; its open tensor map is the identity by the restriction normalization of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], since the open restriction is itself the identity. The exchange for the product projection square with vertical identities is also the identity: in the defining unit--square--counit formula all identity-adjunction maps are identities. Consequently the displayed definition gives $L_{1_T,Z}=1$ and, by conjugating with inverse swaps, $R_{Z,1_T}=1$. Formula (F) now gives $t_{1_{X_1},1_{X_2}}=1_{B_1\boxtimes B_2}$. Compactification compatibility in [fix-prop-projection-formula] and the identity normalization of [thm-sf-comp-composition] identify this computation with the specified comparisons of the statement.
